newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile opens bidding for airport expansion.
newsitem.headline: Chile opens bidding for airport expansion.

text.p: Chile called Tuesday for international bids for a $150 million scheme to expand Santiago's international airport, Aeropuerto Arturo Merino Benitez.

In a statement published in the government's official gazette, the Public Works Ministry said companies which prequalify will receive details of the project from June 18. Offers must be received by August 20.
The scheme calls for expanding the existing terminal, building a new control tower and improving the runways and car parks.

Public Works Deputy Minister Guillermo Pickering said last week that the expansion will improve the passenger terminal and triple cargo capacity at the airport on the city's western outskirts by 1999.
The project is the latest in Chile's push to improve its infrastructure through concessions to private public works companies, some of them foreign.
The winner of the airport concession will carry out the building work, maintain and run the project for an unspecified number of years.
Chile built the existing international terminal in the early 1990s but the sharp increase in air traffic over the last few years has already made it cramped.
